findings.message: The torn orange trail-marker cloth found in gear-search-notice (picked up and pocketed 'just in case') is never referenced again; it is not tracked as an item and has no payoff. ending-1's 'bright patch of orange' is a separate search-team flag, not this cloth. Likewise the remembered marker direction in scout-ahead-notice ('that small fact might matter later') is never used. These read as loose threads for an attentive child reader. Not a blocker since no mechanic depends on them, but narrative-designer should either pay these off or remove the implication that they matter.

late-gear-find and late-clue-find largely re-describe the same scene and object in near-identical phrasing to gear-search and scout-ahead ('half buried in frost', 'the thin, dark crack line', 'the old deer track... might pass below the worst drop'). This is not a structural page revisit (no backward graph edge; these are distinct, newly-written passages, and the graph report confirms the route to every ending is a forward-only DAG with no re-reading of already-visited passages), but the heavy phrase reuse makes the second-look passages feel repetitive on a route that takes both.

Several choice pairs (wrap-snug/wrap-firm, pack-away/double-check, tell-group/study-more, mark-direction/hurry-on, check-russo-first/scan-ridge-first) converge on an identical next passage with no state effect or textual difference. Fine for pacing on a first read, but reduces the sense of agency on a reread; flagging for awareness, not required to fix.

Confirmed example full route: start/tend-ankle -> tend-the-ankle/wrap-snug -> ration-the-food/pack-away -> make-a-plan/check-gear-pile -> gear-search/wrap-pole -> gear-search-notice/pocket-cloth -> gathering/go-get-clue -> late-clue-find/note-crack -> the-long-walk/let-priya-lead -> threshold/cross-gap -> climax-approach/check-russo-first -> climax/splint-move -> ending-1. No route revisits an already-visited passage id to collect an item, clue or reach an ending; graph.r1.json confirms a forward-only reachable DAG (28 explored states, stateSearchComplete true, 5/5 endings reachable, shortestPathToEnding 10, longestSimplePathToEnding 13).

Content integrity: no sexual content, violence/gore, suicide/self-harm or specific-religion references found. No character dies, is frostbitten, or is left behind, matching the brief's 'avoid' list. Vale/Priya/Tomas/Mr. Russo characterization is consistent with brief.continuity.characters throughout (Priya anxious-but-fast, Tomas stubborn-but-steady, Mr. Russo's sprained ankle). Items (ski-pole) and clues (crack-line) are described consistently everywhere they appear and are each meaningfully used at the 'cross-gap' choice, not just collected as filler. The 'go-get-item'/'go-get-clue' locked choices at gathering have fair, specific lockedHints naming exactly why they are locked ('You already checked the gear pile.'), and 'cross-gap' states exactly what is required to unlock it.

Ending count (5) meets the brief's endingTarget (5); route variety for a second read is adequate: two opening orders, two make-a-plan branches with materially different passages, an optional second-fetch decision, and a 4-way climax branch produce meaningfully different playthroughs, not just cosmetic ones.
Literacy/word-set numbers are automated-report output only (reports/validation.r1.json); the literacy.review.status is correctly still 'pending' and this review does not claim a literacy pass.
